## Purpose
`golem-surfaces` provides the communication layer between internal Golem state and external observers. It defines handlers for WebSocket real-time events, Server-Sent Events fallback for HTTP-only clients, Telegram push notifications, and the `GolemSnapshot` type that serializes Golem state across all transport channels.

## Key Invariants
- `GolemSnapshot` serializes deterministically (same Golem state always produces identical JSON)
- WebSocket frames are received in order (enforced by Axum/tokio-tungstenite)
- SSE events conform to EventSource spec: one event per `\n\n` boundary, no colons prefixing field names
- Telegram messages never exceed 4096 characters; truncate or split before sending
- All surfaces emit type-equivalent state information (no transport-specific data loss)
- Handler types implement `Send + Sync` for use in Axum extractors and tokio task spawning
- Connections must authenticate before receiving events; subscription filters are enforced per-connection

## Public API
- `GolemSnapshot` — serializable complete Golem state snapshot (vitality, behavioral phase, PAD vector, activity excerpts, timestamp)
- `WebSocketHandler` — Axum WebSocket upgrade handler factory
- `SseHandler` — Server-Sent Events stream producer for HTTP clients
- `TelegramPusher` — Telegram message dispatcher with rate limiting and backpressure queuing
- `SurfaceEvent` — unified event envelope sent across all surfaces (event type, timestamp, Golem ID, payload)

## Dependencies
None yet. Implementation will require:
- `axum` — web framework and WebSocket/HTTP primitives
- `tokio` — async runtime for handler tasks
- `serde` / `serde_json` — snapshot and event serialization
- `golem_core` — `GolemId`, `BehavioralPhase`, event types
- `golem_mortality` — `VitalityState` for snapshots
- `golem_daimon` — `PadVector` for emotional state in snapshots

## Implementation Notes
- WebSocket and SSE handlers must spawn tokio tasks; never block the event loop with synchronous I/O
- SSE requires `Content-Type: text/event-stream` response header and `\n\n` event terminators
- Telegram queue must be bounded (e.g., 100 pending messages); drop oldest on overflow rather than blocking
- `GolemSnapshot` should include: vitality state (composite score and three-clock values), current phase, PAD vector, last 5 activity records, snapshot creation timestamp
- Apply privacy filtering before snapshot creation; redact sensitive fields unless client has explicit consent scope
- Use `tracing` crate for logging (debug level for connection lifecycle, warn for transport errors)
- Prefer `axum::extract::ws` for WebSocket if Axum version supports it; otherwise `tokio-tungstenite`

## Test Requirements
- Snapshot round-trip serialization: `test_golem_snapshot_serde_round_trip` in `tests/serialization.rs`
- SSE event format: `test_sse_event_format_compliant` (events end with `\n\n`, field names have no colons)
- Telegram truncation: `test_telegram_message_truncated_at_4096_chars`
- Frame ordering: unit test verifying WebSocket frames arrive in order
- All snapshot mandatory fields present: vitality, phase, pad_vector, timestamp

## Do Not
- Don't serialize internal types directly; always go through `GolemSnapshot` with privacy filtering
- Don't implement blocking I/O in WebSocket or SSE handlers; offload to bounded channels
- Don't accept unbounded JSON payloads; validate size before parsing
- Don't buffer unbounded event queues; use bounded channels and apply backpressure
